PART I

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

Our financial and operating results are subject to a variety of risks inherent in the global oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses and many of them are not within our control.

Supply and Demand

Economic conditions. The demand for energy and petrochemicals is generally linked closely with broad-based economic activities and levels of prosperity, so recessions or periods of low or negative economic growth will typically have a direct adverse impact on our results. Other factors that affect general economic conditions in the world or in a major region can also impact the demand for energy.

Competition could adversely impact our market share and financial results.

Our target markets remain competitive, and competition may intensify with expanding and changing product and service offerings, industry standards, customer needs, new entrants and consolidations, so our market share and financial results could suffer if we do not compete effectively in every one of these markets.

See Item 1C for our cybersecurity risk management, which is described there in detail.

Item 1C

Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt our operations, and attempted cyber disruptions from a variety of sources including state-sponsored actors happen regularly and increasingly; these could result in loss of data, regulatory penalties and remediation costs.
